newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rupee ends down in kerb, seen falling.

text.p: The Pakistani rupee ended 0.02 down at 41.00 to the dollar in the kerb market on Wednesday as dollar demand edged ahead of supply from abroad, dealers said.
The rupee is likely to open lower on Monday after a four-day break for the Moslem Eid al-Adha festival, one dealer said.
The State (central) bank of Pakistan rate, last changed on October 22, was 40.1200/40.3206 to the dollar.
The premium on the foreign exchange bearer certificates closed at 2.40 percent compared to the opening at 2.30 percent.
